caching.title: Local Cache
caching.description: Cache responses locally with two complementary lookup paths: direct hash matching for exact replays, and semantic similarity search for related content.
caching.enableHelp: Loads (or unloads) the plugin without a server restart. Configuration changes you make below mutate the live plugin in place, no redeploy needed.
caching.directHelp: Direct-only mode hashes each request and replays an exact match. No embeddings, no provider needed. Cheapest path, perfect for stable prompts.
caching.semanticHelp: Direct + semantic mode adds vector similarity search on top of direct hash matching. Requires an embedding-capable provider and the model's real dimension. Direct hits are still served first; semantic search runs only when the direct lookup misses.
caching.structuralChangeHelp: <b0>Heads up:</b0> a vector store namespace can only hold vectors of <em1>one</em1> dimension. Whenever you change the embedding <b2>provider</b2>, <b3>model</b3>, or <b4>dimension</b4>, make sure the <b5>dimension</b5> still matches what the model produces, otherwise writes to the existing namespace will fail and reads will silently miss. The namespace is <em6>not</em6> recreated automatically; either use a fresh namespace or drop the existing class/index in your vector store before saving.
caching.inheritedKeysHelp: API keys are inherited from the embedding provider's main configuration, you don't need to add them again here.
caching.dimensionHelp: Vector size produced by the embedding model. Must match the model exactly (e.g. <code0>1536</code0> for OpenAI <code1>text-embedding-3-small</code1>, <code2>3072</code2> for <code3>text-embedding-3-large</code3>, <code4>768</code4> for many Cohere/Voyage models).
caching.ttlHelp: How long cached entries live before they expire. Override per-request via the <b0>x-bf-cache-ttl</b0> header.
caching.thresholdHelp: Minimum cosine similarity for a semantic hit. Override per-request via <b0>x-bf-cache-threshold</b0>.
caching.namespaceHelp: Bucket/index name where cache entries live. Leave blank to use the default (<code0>BifrostLocalCachePlugin</code0>). Changing this points the plugin at a different (possibly empty) bucket. Old entries are not deleted, they just stop being queried.
caching.defaultKeyHelp: Fallback partition key used when a request doesn't set <b0>x-bf-cache-key</b0>. Cache keys isolate entries: same key ↔ shared cache pool. Leave blank to <b1>disable caching</b1> for any request that doesn't send the header.
caching.conversationThresholdHelp: Skip caching for conversations with more than this many messages. Long histories rarely match exactly and inflate the cache without paying off.
caching.cacheByModelHelp: Include model name in the cache key. Different models won't share cached responses.
caching.cacheByProviderHelp: Include provider name in the cache key. Different providers won't share cached responses.

overrides.key: <b0>x-bf-cache-key</b0>: scope this request to a specific cache partition.
overrides.ttl: <b0>x-bf-cache-ttl</b0>: override TTL for just this request.
overrides.type: <b0>x-bf-cache-type</b0>: send <code1>direct</code1> or <code2>semantic</code2> to limit lookup to one path.
overrides.noStore: <b0>x-bf-cache-no-store</b0>: <code1>true</code1> to skip writing the response (still serves cached hits).

caching.excludeSystemPromptHelp: Strip system messages from the cache key.
caching.semanticProviderRequired: Configure an embedding-capable provider to enable semantic mode.
caching.searchEmbeddingModel: Search or type an embedding model...

security.title: Security Settings
security.description: Configure security and access control settings.
security.setupTokenHelp: Enter the setup token configured by your operator to create the first admin account. It's set via setup_token in config.json or the BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN environment variable.
security.setupTokenPlaceholder: Paste the setup token configured by your operator
security.enableAuthHelp: Require authentication (virtual key, API key, or user token) for all inference endpoints.
security.enforceVkHelp: Require a virtual key for all inference requests.
security.allowedHeadersHelp: Comma-separated list of allowed headers for CORS.
security.toastInvalidOrigins: Invalid origins: {{origins}}. Origins must be valid URLs like https://example.com, wildcard patterns like https://*.example.com, or "*" to allow all origins
security.toastInvalidCooldown: Rotation cooldown must be a duration like "30s", "5m", or "1h30m" (leave empty to disable).
security.vkRotationCooldownDesc: After rotating a virtual key, the previous value keeps authenticating for this long, giving callers time to switch to the new key. Use a duration like 30s, 5m, or 1h. Leave empty (or 0) to have the old value stop working immediately. Maximum 30 days.
security.authTypeUnavailable: Could not load authentication type. Dashboard password settings are hidden until this request succeeds.
security.passwordProtectHelp: Set up authentication credentials to protect your Bifrost dashboard. Once configured, use the generated token for all admin API calls.
security.passwordPolicyHelp: Use at least 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character. Env var references are accepted.
security.firstSetupHelp: No admin account exists yet, so this instance is reachable without a password. To finish setup, ask your operator for the setup token configured via <code0>setup_token</code0> in <code1>config.json</code1> (or the  <code2>BIFROST_SETUP_TOKEN</code2> environment variable) and paste it here.
security.dualCredentialHelp: How to handle inference requests that present both an identity provider access token (<b0>Authorization: Bearer</b0>) and a virtual key (<b1>x-bf-vk</b1>). <b2>Prefer IDP token</b2> uses the user token for identity, <b3>Prefer virtual key</b3> drops the IDP token and authenticates via the virtual key, and <b4>Reject request</b4> returns a 400 error.
security.directKeysHelp: When enabled, callers can pass a provider API key directly in the <b0>Authorization</b0>, <b1>x-api-key</b1>, or  <b2>x-goog-api-key</b2> header alongside <b3>x-bf-direct-key: true</b3>. Bifrost will use that key directly, bypassing the registered key pool.
security.originsHelp: Comma-separated list of allowed origins for CORS and WebSocket connections. Localhost origins are always allowed. Each origin must be a complete URL with protocol (e.g., https://app.example.com, http://10.0.0.100:3000). Wildcards are supported for subdomains (e.g., https://*.example.com) or use "*" to allow all origins.
security.requiredHeadersHelp: Comma-separated list of headers that must be present on every request. Requests missing any of these headers will be rejected with a 400 error. Header names are case-insensitive.
security.routesHelp: Comma-separated list of routes that bypass the auth middleware. Requests to these routes will not require authentication. System routes like <b0>/health</b0>, <b1>/api/session/login</b1>, and <b2>/api/session/is-auth-enabled</b2> are always whitelisted regardless of this setting.

logging.title: Logs Settings
logging.description: Configure logging settings for requests and responses.
logging.enableLogsHelp: Enable logging of requests and responses to a SQL database. This can add 40-60mb of overhead to the system memory.
logging.requiresStore: Requires logs store to be configured and enabled in config.json.
logging.disableContentLoggingHelp: When enabled, only usage metadata (latency, cost, token count, status, routing IDs, etc.) is logged. Request/response content (messages, params, tool calls, and any raw provider bytes) is dropped from log records, even when store_raw_request_response is on. Raw-byte send-back to callers via send_back_raw_* is unaffected.
logging.retainContentHelp: When enabled, requests with content logging disabled (via the global setting above or the x-bf-disable-content-logging header) still have their full content offloaded to object storage, but the content is never shown in logs: the database row stays metadata-only and the UI/API never fetch the payload back. Content is then only readable with direct access to the storage bucket. When disabled, content for such requests is dropped entirely (current behavior).
logging.requiresObjectStorage: Requires object storage to be configured on the logs store in config.json.
logging.allowContentOverrideHelp: When enabled, individual requests can override the global content logging setting using the x-bf-disable-content-logging header or context key, and can opt-in to persisting raw provider bytes in logs using the x-bf-store-raw-request-response header. Raw-byte storage requires content logging to be on, either globally, or via x-bf-disable-content-logging: false on the same request. If content logging is off, raw bytes are dropped from the log record even when x-bf-store-raw-request-response: true. Does not control sending raw bytes back to callers; see {{setting}}.
logging.allowRawOverrideHelp: When enabled, individual requests can send raw provider request/response bytes back to the caller using the x-bf-send-back-raw-request and x-bf-send-back-raw-response headers. Does not affect log storage; raw-byte persistence in logs is controlled by {{setting}}.
logging.logRetentionDaysHelp: Number of days to retain logs in the database. Minimum is 1 day. Older logs will be automatically deleted.
logging.hideDeletedVks: Do Not Show Deleted VirtualKeys In Filters
logging.hideDeletedVksHelp: When enabled, deleted virtual keys are excluded from Virtual Keys filter options in Logs, Dashboard, and MCP Logs.
logging.loggingHeadersHelp: Comma-separated list of request headers to capture in log metadata. Supports exact names and wildcard patterns (e.g. x-custom-* captures all headers with that prefix, * logs all headers; note that * will capture sensitive headers like Authorization). Values are extracted from incoming requests and stored in the metadata field of log entries. Headers with the x-bf-lh- prefix are always captured automatically.
logging.toastRetentionMin: Log retention days must be at least 1 day
logging.hiddenRequestTypesHelp: Selected request types are still logged but excluded from Logs and Dashboard views, including counts, charts and filter options. Streaming and non-streaming types are separate. Leave empty to show every request type. Takes effect on the next request, no restart needed. Can also be set with

mcpSettings.title: MCP Settings
mcpSettings.description: Configure MCP (Model Context Protocol) agent and tool settings.
mcpSettings.maxAgentDepthHelp: Maximum depth for MCP agent execution.
mcpSettings.toolTimeoutHelp: Maximum time in seconds for tool execution.
mcpSettings.toastDepthPositive: Max agent depth must be a positive number.
mcpSettings.toastTimeoutPositive: Tool execution timeout must be a positive number.
mcpSettings.toastAuthCodeTtl: Authorization code TTL must be between 1 and 900 seconds (15 minutes).
mcpSettings.toastAccessTokenTtl: Access token TTL must be at least 60 seconds.
mcpSettings.maxDepthHelp: Maximum depth for MCP agent execution.
mcpSettings.refreshIntervalHelp: How often to refresh tool lists from MCP servers. Set to 0 to use the default of 10 minutes.
mcpSettings.disableAutoToolInjectionHelp: When enabled, MCP tools are not automatically included in every request. Tools are only injected when explicitly specified via request headers (<code0>x-bf-mcp-include-tools</code0>) and still must be allowed by the virtual key MCP configuration.
mcpSettings.tempTokenHelp: When enabled, per-user MCP OAuth links can include a short-lived scoped token so someone without an active Bifrost dashboard session can complete the flow. Keep disabled to require normal dashboard authentication.
mcpSettings.bindingHelp: How tools are exposed in the VFS: server-level (all tools per server) or tool-level (individual tools).
mcpSettings.externalClientUrlHelp: Override Bifrost's public base URL when it runs behind a reverse proxy. <b0>Leave blank to derive the URL</b0> from the incoming <code1>Host</code1> header. Used as the <code2>redirect_uri</code2> Bifrost registers with upstream OAuth providers when it acts as a client to an MCP server (e.g. Notion or Jira redirect the browser to <code3><URL>/api/oauth/callback</code3> after login). Supports env var syntax (e.g.  <code4>env.BIFROST_EXTERNAL_URL</code4>).
mcpSettings.externalClientUrlWarningHelp: Upstream OAuth providers lock the <code0>redirect_uri</code0> to whatever was registered initially, so MCP clients that already completed OAuth will fail with <em1>"Invalid redirect URI"</em1>. To recover, clear the stored OAuth client credentials for the affected MCP servers and re-authorize so Bifrost re-runs Dynamic Client Registration with the new URL.
mcpSettings.authModeHelp: Controls how inbound MCP clients (e.g. Claude Code, Cursor) authenticate to the <code0>/mcp</code0>  endpoint. <b1>headers</b1> (default) - VK / api-key / session headers only, OAuth discovery disabled. <b2>both</b2> - accepts header credentials and Bifrost-issued JWTs; existing integrations are unaffected. <b3>oauth</b3> - JWTs only; VK and header access is disabled.
mcpSettings.issuerUrlHelp: Stable public URL advertised in discovery documents and embedded as the <code0>iss</code0> claim in every JWT. Leave blank to derive it from the request <code1>Host</code1> header (sufficient for most deployments). Multi-host or reverse-proxy deployments might need this. Supports env var syntax (e.g.  <code2>env.BIFROST_ISSUER_URL</code2>).
mcpSettings.authCodeTtlHelp: How long the one-time code is valid after the consent page redirects back to the MCP client (default: 300, max 900 = 15 min).
mcpSettings.accessTokenTtlHelp: Lifetime of issued JWT Bearer tokens. Clients silently refresh when expired (default: 600 = 10 min). Also bounds how long a revoked grant keeps working before it is cut off.
mcpSettings.requireIdpLoginHelp: When enabled, the OAuth consent flow only offers identity-provider login. Virtual keys can no longer be used to obtain an MCP token, and existing virtual-key OAuth sessions lose access immediately. Anonymous session access is unaffected (controlled by Enforce Authentication on Inference).
mcpSettings.allToolsPerServerInASinglePyFile: All tools per server in a single .py file
mcpSettings.externalClientUrlWarning: Changing this URL can break existing MCP clients
mcpSettings.headerAccessDisabled: VK / header MCP access will be disabled
mcpSettings.headerAccessDisabledHelp: All existing MCP integrations that use a virtual key, api-key, or session header will stop working immediately. Clients must re-authenticate via the OAuth consent flow to obtain a JWT before they can connect.
mcpSettings.oauthDiscoveryDisabledHelp: All MCP clients that authenticated via the OAuth consent flow will lose access; their JWTs will be rejected and their refresh tokens will become unusable. They will need to reconfigure using a virtual key or api-key header.
mcpSettings.bothAuthModesHelp: Existing VK / header integrations continue to work unchanged. New MCP clients can connect via OAuth - they'll be redirected to the consent page to pick an identity.
mcpSettings.virtualKeyOauthDisabled: Virtual-key MCP access via OAuth will stop
mcpSettings.virtualKeyOauthDisabledHelp: MCP clients that authenticated with a virtual key will lose access immediately and must sign in through your identity provider to reconnect.
